name: op_resize_no_dom_rebuild
description: THE RESIZE POLICY (user ruling 2026-08-08): a resize NEVER re-invokes the app's layout() — dom_regenerations stays 0 — unless it crosses a boundary the callback can observe (a CSS_BREAKPOINTS threshold, an orientation flip, or a recorded window_width_*/window_height_* query answer). Background: a Wayland drag delivers one configure PER PIXEL (373 measured in 5 s) and each full regeneration cost 654-942 ms, so the pre-fix pipeline could repaint ~1.4x/second during a drag. Sizes are chosen against CSS_BREAKPOINTS = [320, 480, 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920]: 800->900->850 stays inside (768, 1024] on the width axis and crosses nothing on the height axis, so both resizes must be pure relayouts (exact_dom_regens 0, layout still ran: min_layout_passes 1). 900->1100 crosses 1024, so exactly one full regeneration must follow. If the first assert fails with dom_regens > 0, the fast path regressed — check the escalation site in e2e/runner.rs service() and LayoutWindow::resize_needs_full_regeneration. If the second fails with 0, the boundary detection regressed and apps CANNOT switch mobile/desktop DOMs any more, which is worse than slow.
